ref_speedup_note: Anchor 3.16 calibrated in oracle mode on NVIDIA H20. tests/ref_speedup.txt is authoritative at scoring; this file is only the in-image fallback. See tests/ref_speedup.caveat.md to re-measure on your hardware.
value_axis: achieved_global_memory_bandwidth (memory-bound; wall-time tracks it). gpu_bench.py prints achieved-GB/s per shape as work evidence. NOTE: the bytes moved are IDENTICAL for a coalesced vs a strided kernel, so a bytes-moved proxy alone cannot discriminate them — the scored metric MUST be wall-time / achieved bandwidth.
compile_note: transpose.py JIT-compiles transpose_kernel.cu with nvcc (torch cpp-extension) at scoring; a changed .cu forces a fresh recompile. Requires nvcc + CUDA headers (cuda_fp16.h, cuda_runtime.h) + ninja in the image (see the Dockerfile build notes); H20 = sm_90; -ccbin g++-11 fallback. No mma.h needed (this is data movement, not a matrix instruction).
